transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, what finally made me come in is that I just keep forgetting really basic adult things. It's... it's getting bad. Like paying bills, returning emails for job interviews, or even just showing up for appointments and following through on everyday errands. I just forget. And it's started costing me real opportunities now, so... I knew I needed to get some help.
Have you been feeling overwhelmed or stressed about these forgetful incidents?

Um... I'm not really sure. I don't know if I'd say I feel overwhelmed, exactly. I mean, it's definitely frustrating, and I know it's a big problem since I'm losing out on jobs and stuff. But I haven't really stopped to think about my stress levels specifically. I mostly just know that it keeps happening and I need to figure out how to stop it.
Have you been feeling sad or down about your situation?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad. I mean... I'm definitely annoyed with myself, but I don't feel depressed or down about it. It's just a problem I need to fix, you know? I don't feel like crying or anything like that, it's just really inconvenient.
Have you been feeling anxious about anything lately?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel anxious or nervous about things. I'm not sitting around worrying all the time. It's really just the forgetting things that's the issue. I just... I just want to figure out why my brain keeps dropping the ball on stuff I need to do.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?

Yeah, I definitely do. Like, I'll sit down to update my resume or work on a coding practice problem, and... a text notification will go off, or I'll hear someone talking outside. Sometimes it's even just a random thought about another task popping into my head. But whatever it is, it just pulls me completely off track before I even notice what happened.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Yeah, definitely. If I have to sit through an interview, or a meeting... or even just a movie, really, I get this... this pressure inside my body. It's like I just need to get up, or shift around, or do something with my hands. If I have to just sit perfectly still, I feel like I'm going to crawl right out of my skin.
When did you first start noticing these problems with forgetting things and having trouble focusing?

Honestly, it goes way back. Even in elementary school, my teachers would always write notes saying I was a bright kid, but... I was constantly losing my worksheets. I would rush through the directions, talk out of turn a lot, and my desk was always just so messy that I could never actually find my assignments when I needed them. So, yeah, it's been happening since I was little.
Do you have trouble with forgetting things and focusing at work or school, and also when you're doing things you enjoy or find interesting?

Yeah, it really affects both. I actually got fired from my last job, so I'm unemployed right now. And even while trying to find a new one... I've completely missed important interview follow-ups. 

And as for things I enjoy or find interesting... um, well, I was doing this volunteer project that I really cared about, but I was struggling so much to keep track of things that I had to step back from it completely. Honestly, it's just really frustrating because I feel like I can't reliably manage the basic steps of moving my life forward right now.
Have you experienced these problems with forgetting things and having trouble focusing consistently throughout your life, or have they varied in severity over time?

Well, like I mentioned, I've always had some issues since I was a kid, but the severity has definitely changed. It's been seriously affecting me for about a year and two months now. That's around when things really started falling apart at my biotech job, and it's just continued being this bad ever since I got fired.
Have you ever had difficulty following rules or respecting social norms?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't go out of my way to break rules or, like, do things that are socially inappropriate on purpose. I might accidentally interrupt someone because I get too eager to say something, or I might forget a rule because I wasn't paying close enough attention, but it's never about disrespecting the rules or norms themselves. I definitely try to follow them.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences?

Um, not really in a big way. I mean, I might buy something small without thinking about it, or like I said, I'll blurt something out in a conversation before I realize I'm interrupting. But I don't do anything dangerous or make huge decisions completely on a whim. It's more just... little things in the moment that I don't catch myself on.
As a child, were you often described as being overly physically active, such as running, climbing, or having trouble playing quietly?

No, I wouldn't say I was overly active like that. I didn't really run around or climb on things all the time, and I didn't have any particular trouble playing quietly. I was more just disorganized and easily distracted, rather than physically hyperactive.
Have your difficulties with forgetting things and focusing affected your relationships with friends or family?

No, I haven't really noticed that. My friends and family know I can be a bit scatterbrained, but it hasn't caused any real issues or fights. They usually just remind me if I forget something. So, no, I wouldn't say it's affected my relationships.
Have you experienced difficulties with focusing and forgetting things in multiple settings, such as at home, at work, or in social situations?

Um, honestly, I don't really think so. Like, I know I struggle with focusing and keeping track of things, but I haven't really noticed it being a huge problem across the board. Maybe a little bit at home, but I wouldn't say it's happening everywhere I go or in every situation. I'm not entirely sure, to be honest.
Have you ever lost a friend or had trouble making friends because of your difficulties with focusing or forgetting things?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've never actually lost a friend over it, and making friends hasn't really been an issue. Like I said, people around me just kind of accept that I forget things sometimes. It hasn't really gotten in the way of my social life.
Have you often felt excessively fidgety or restless as an adult?

Yeah, I do. Um, when I have to sit through an interview, or a meeting, or even just a movie, I get this... this pressure inside my body. It's like I absolutely need to get up, shift around, or do something with my hands. If I have to just sit perfectly still, I feel like I'm going to crawl right out of my skin.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with focusing, forgetfulness, or restlessness consistently from childhood into adulthood?

Yeah, definitely. It's been happening for as long as I can remember. Um, even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write notes saying that I was bright, but I constantly lost my worksheets. They said I rushed through directions and talked out of turn a lot, too. And my desk was always so messy that I could never actually find my assignments when I needed them. So, yeah, it's definitely been a consistent thing since I was little.
Do you have trouble with impulsivity or blurting out answers in multiple settings, like at work, at home, or with friends?

Yeah, I do. Um, in regular conversations or even in interviews, I tend to jump in before the other person is actually done talking. I usually do it because I think I know exactly where they are going with their sentence, so I just start answering. But then I realize I completely cut them off, or... or I end up answering the wrong question entirely because I didn't wait to hear the whole thing.
Have you experienced difficulties with focusing or paying attention in multiple settings, such as at home, at work, or in social situations?

Um, no, not really. I haven't really noticed having trouble with that. Like, I know I just said I get restless and tend to interrupt people, but as far as actually focusing or paying attention... I don't think I really struggle with that at home or when I'm hanging out with friends. So, no, that hasn't really been an issue for me.
Have your symptoms of forgetfulness, difficulty focusing, and restlessness significantly impacted your ability to function in your daily life or maintain employment?

Yeah, it really has. Um, I actually got fired. And since getting fired, I've completely missed follow-ups for other interviews. I also had to step back from a volunteer project that I really cared about because I just couldn't keep up with it. So right now, I'm just unemployed and... I don't know, I just feel like I can't reliably manage the basic steps of moving my life forward.
